facts: $\text{speed}=\dfrac{\text{distance covered}}{\text{time taken}}$ for a straight segment. On a return, use the size of the distance change.
Always check the scale on **both** axes before reading a value — one grid square is rarely one unit.
For a segment that does not start at the origin, use the distance **change** and the time **change**, not the end readings.
If the time axis is in minutes, convert to hours before giving a speed in km/h: $20$ min $=\frac{1}{3}$ h.
steps: Read the two end points of the segment from the axes.
Find the change in distance and the change in time.
Divide the change in distance by the change in time.

workedExamples.solution_text:
Read the endpoints and use distance covered divided by time taken.
(a) From $(0,0)$ to $(2,14)$: $s=14\div2=7$ km/h.
(b) From $(2,14)$ to $(3,14)$ the distance does not change, so $s=0$ km/h.
(c) From $(3,14)$ to $(5,34)$: distance $=34-14=20$ km; time $=5-3=2$ h.
$s=20\div2=10$ km/h. Use the changes, rather than the final readings.

Read each moving stage’s endpoints.
(a) The return goes from $(1.5,18)$ to $(3,0)$: distance covered $=18-0=18$ km and time $=3-1.5=1.5$ h.
$s=18\div1.5=12$ km/h. The falling line does not mean negative speed.
(b) Outward speed $=18\div1=18$ km/h.
$18-12=6$ km/h, so the outward stage was faster by $6$ km/h.

Read the final stage’s endpoints: $(15,1500)$ and $(30,4500)$.
Distance covered $=4500-1500=3000$ m $=3$ km.
Time $=30-15=15$ min $=\frac{15}{60}=0.25$ h.
$s=3\div0.25=12$ km/h.

Read each cyclist’s moving segment from the common axes.
(a) A: $s=27\div3=9$ km/h.
B: $s=21\div1.5=14$ km/h; the horizontal stage is a stop and is not included in riding time.
(b) $14-9=5$ km/h, so B was riding $5$ km/h faster.

development.solution_text:
$s_{1}=\frac{80-0}{1-0}$
$=80\text{ km/h}$
$s_{2}=\frac{200-80}{4-2}$
$=60\text{ km/h}$
$80-60=20$, so the train was $20$ km/h faster before the stop.

$s_{\text{Theo}}=\frac{50-0}{2-0}$
$=25\text{ km/h}$
$s_{\text{Rani}}=\frac{60}{4}$
$=15\text{ km/h}$
$25-15=10$, so Theo was riding $10$ km/h faster than Rani.

mastery.solution_text:
$s_{\text{before}}=\frac{50-0}{1-0}$
$=50\text{ km/h}$
$s_{\text{after}}=\frac{140-50}{4-2}$
$=\frac{90}{2}$
$=45\text{ km/h}$
$45<50$, so Marisol is wrong — she was $5$ km/h slower after the stop.

$s_{\text{Amara}}=\frac{72-36}{2-0}$
$=\frac{36}{2}$
$=18\text{ km/h}$
$s_{\text{Kwame}}=\frac{72-24}{2-0}$
$=\frac{48}{2}$
$=24\text{ km/h}$
$24-18=6$, so Kwame was riding $6$ km/h faster.
